title: Volve (real data): unwinding shells, 2002 and 2010 per trace

notes: amplitudes are relative; compare within this file only

phase is the unwrapped instantaneous phase of the analytic signal: one turn per cycle of the wavelet; instantaneous frequency is its rate and is meaningless where the envelope is below 20% of the trace's maximum

the monitor is read at the base's traces, moved by +2.86 ms and scaled by 1.33, both measured over 600-1400 where nothing in the earth should have changed (median lag of 6 trace pairs; a constant offset between two processings is not a change in the earth)
the grain: after those corrections the two vintages still differ by an NRMS of 0.38 (correlation 0.92) in that window; a difference deeper down must be read against it
6 traces on a 2 x 3 grid, 600-2900 ms

Volve ST10010 PSDM full stack (3-41 degrees), depth-to-time converted, 4 ms; domain TIME and quantity AMPLITUDE as stated by the user from the text header; polarity unknown (not stated in the headers)
time-vs-depth check (seismic_lib): leans time; the cube is blank above about 196 ms (shallow mute), so its own seabed cannot be used
water bottom from the interpreters' horizons: 111 ms TWT and 91 m depth over the survey; read as time it implies 82 m of water, read as depth 111 m: only time fits
both volumes are PZ full-angle PSDM stacks converted to time, 4 ms, on the same grid; shot with different cable layouts and sources eight years apart

the second spiral is the monitor's instantaneous phase on the same radius; the opening between the spirals is the monitor's phase minus the base's, positive where the monitor lags (its event is later); a lag of 2 to 3 ms at 30 Hz is 20 to 30 degrees of turn
source_label: base ST0202, full stack, PSDM Kirchhoff, name ends _T; monitor ST10010, full stack, PSDM Kirchhoff, name ends _T
